provenance.note: Curated flagship register. Each body carries its own document links and source ids; page numbers in the text are printed pages unless marked PDF.

note: Nagpur has no public lake register with areas. History comes from the Imperial Gazetteer (1908), the Maharashtra District Gazetteer (1966) and the Supreme Court's 2025 judgment on Futala; dam data from CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019); current work from NMC's Environment Status Reports, the State's Government Resolutions, the AMRUT 2.0 portal and NMC's budgets. Entries are graded V (verified against a primary document), N (single source) or C (claim only); every entry here is V. Areas are given only where an official register states one: Ambazari's 378 acres and Gorewada's 474 acres are CWC's 153 and 192 hectares. Ownership is recorded differently by different documents: CWC's register names the State Water Resources Department as operator of Ambazari and Gorewada, while the High Court records Ambazari dam as NMC's property; each claim is shown with its source. NMC's 2023-24 report counts 11 lakes; the three not listed here (Binaki, Pandharabodi and Police Line Takli) have no history in the documents read. Locations are NMC's 2023-24 sampling points, except Lendi, placed at the centre of its MRSAC 2017-18 polygon.

bodies.name: Futala Lake
bodies.builder: Gyanoji Bhosale, in 1799 (Supreme Court of India, 2025, para 5.3)
bodies.feed: the Futala stream, dammed to form the lake, which collects water from the slopes of Seminary Hills and is a tributary of the Nag (the Supreme Court, quoting the Nagpur Museum's record)
bodies.status: On 7 October 2025 the Supreme Court held that Futala is a man-made water body built for irrigation and drinking water, and so not a 'wetland' under the Wetlands Rules, 2017. It upheld the High Court's directions of 30 November 2023: no permanent construction within the lake, and NMC and Maha Metro to keep the water body clean. In the National Green Tribunal's case on the lake's condition, the order of 10 September 2026 recorded NMC's technical sanction of Rs 33,09,488 for a sewer for the settlement beside the lake, and the case was next listed for 29 October 2026. NMC's 2023-24 sampling recorded water hyacinth on the lake.
bodies.cultural_note: The Supreme Court records that the lake 'along with its catchment' covers about 200 hectares; a Nagpur Museum record quoted in the judgment says it was built to give water to the Telankhedi precinct, a garden of the Bhonsle rulers with a guest house for dignitaries. The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer counts the Telinkheri reservoir among the 'worthy monuments of the best period of Bhonsla rule'. The 1966 District Gazetteer describes the Telankhedi tank's 725.6 m main dam and the 34.4 hectares of the Government Agriculture College farm and Telankhedi garden it irrigated.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point FL

bodies.name: Ambazari Lake
bodies.era: Bhonsle-era tank, raised and piped in 1873
bodies.builder: not named; built in the days of Bhonsle rule (1966 District Gazetteer); in 1873 the municipality raised the old tank's embankment by 17 feet and laid pipes to carry its water to the city by gravity, at a cost of Rs 4 lakh
bodies.feed: the upper Nag, which leaves the lake as the river through the city (the 1966 Gazetteer: 'almost a natural reservoir formed in the basin of the Nag river')
bodies.status: CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019) lists the dam as completed in 1870: earthfill, 13.71 m high and 952.51 m long, holding 8.37 million cubic metres over 153 hectares, operated by the State Water Resources Department and registered for irrigation. After the overflow of 23 September 2023, in which four people died according to the Collector's affidavit, the High Court is overseeing safety works (PIL 56/2023): the Irrigation Department told the court in February 2024 that the design of three 4 m by 2.5 m spillway gates was in progress, and on 2 July 2025 the court recorded that the dam's safety is NMC's responsibility as its owner. NMC's 2023-24 sampling recorded water hyacinth and greenish water.
bodies.cultural_note: The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer records the embankment raised again by famine labour in 1900, to 1,033 yards long and 35 feet high, with a water surface of 412 acres, and that a surface drainage scheme was taken up to keep the piped supply from waterlogging the city. The 1966 District Gazetteer calls Ambazari the oldest lake of its type in Nagpur, 'built in the days of the Bhosle rule', and gives its daily draw then as over 10 million litres.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point AZ-1
bodies.area_note: 378 acres = 153 ha, CWC register 2019 (gross storage 8.37 Mm3); 412 acres of water surface in the 1908 Imperial Gazetteer

bodies.name: Gorewada Lake
bodies.builder: not named in the sources; built as the city's second source after Ambazari's supply 'was inadequate to meet the demand' (1966 District Gazetteer)
bodies.feed: the Pili river ('Poli River' in CWC's register), dammed by an earthen embankment
bodies.status: CWC's National Register of Large Dams (2019) lists the dam as completed in 1911: earthfill, 17.37 m high and 710 m long, holding 8.84 million cubic metres over 192 hectares, operated by the State Water Resources Department and registered for irrigation. NMC's 2023-24 sampling recorded plastics and weeds at the bank. One of NMC's three artificial idol-immersion tanks, used in Ganeshotsav 2025, is in Gorewada village (survey no. 106; estimated at Rs 19.62 crore, including works around it).
bodies.cultural_note: In 1966 the District Gazetteer gave its capacity as 275.32 million cubic feet above filter level and its daily draw as 18.20 million litres, through three filters beside the reservoir.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point GD
bodies.area_note: 474 acres = 192 ha, CWC register 2019 (gross storage 8.84 Mm3)

bodies.name: Gandhisagar Lake
bodies.builder: the Bhonsle rulers ('a large rectangular lake built by the Bhosles and improved in later years', 1966 District Gazetteer); no individual builder or year is named
bodies.status: NMC's 2023-24 report records the first phase of development as complete and a second phase under way: desilting, a walking track, a rainwater drain, edge and retaining walls, a toilet block, a sewage treatment plant, fountains, a footbridge and parking. NMC's 2022-23 report had set 2024 as the target for this lake, Sonegaon and Sakkardara. NMC's 2026-27 budget provides Rs 1 crore as its share of the lake's rejuvenation; no State sanction for the lake was found.
bodies.cultural_note: The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer places the Juma talao 'between the city and the railway station' among the monuments of the best period of Bhonsla rule. In 1966 the District Gazetteer described a garden with a small temple in the middle of the lake, and its fisheries list already used the name Gandhi Sagar.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point GS

bodies.name: Sonegaon Lake
bodies.era: Described by the State as 'ancient and historic'
bodies.status: Beautification in two phases: phase 1 under the State's basic-amenities scheme (Rs 17.32 crore, sanctioned 28 February 2019) and phase 2 under the Tourism Department (Rs 24.96 crore, 7 November 2023). NMC's 2023-24 report records phase 1 complete and phase 2 under way; NMC's 2026-27 budget provides Rs 12 crore. In November 2025 the High Court opened a case on its own motion over backwater from the lake entering homes.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point SG-1

bodies.name: Sakkardara Lake
bodies.status: NMC's 2023-24 report records the first phase of development complete and a second phase under way. On 10 July 2026 the State sanctioned Rs 20 crore of its own funds for works at the lake, to be executed by the Nagpur Improvement Trust.
bodies.cultural_note: The 1908 Imperial Gazetteer mentions the Sakardara Bagh 'about a mile from the city', with a small menagerie; the 1966 District Gazetteer lists Sakkardara among the city's old gardens.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point SD

bodies.name: Naik Lake
bodies.status: Rejuvenation sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0 on 2 November 2022 at Rs 12.95 crore, with completion expected in 12 months. NMC's 2023-24 report records the first phase as complete; the AMRUT 2.0 portal lists the project as 'Project Completed' at Rs 15.95 crore (read 15 October 2026; the portal gives no dates). NMC's sampling recorded water hyacinth. The lake lies downstream of Lendi lake.
bodies.coord_source: NMC Environment Status Report 2023-24, Table 6.4 (printed p.141), sampling point NK

bodies.name: Lendi Lake
bodies.status: Rejuvenation sanctioned under AMRUT 2.0 on 2 November 2022 at Rs 14.13 crore, with completion expected in 12 months. NMC's 2023-24 report records that the development work 'was not completed on account of opposition from residents to removal of encroachment', and that the lake was not sampled because of dense vegetation and low water. It is not among the Nagpur projects on the AMRUT 2.0 portal (October 2026).
bodies.coord_source: Centroid of MRSAC 1:10,000 water-body polygon 505040320101969 (2017-18); NMC's 2023-24 report has no sampling point here
